summary: Anne Casile is a scholar in indology and archaeology who studied under Claudine Bautze-Picron. She served as an AHRC research assistant at the British Museum (circa 2008–2011) and held a post at the French National Research Institute for Sustainable Development (circa 2011).

Anne E. Monius was a scholar of indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her undergraduate, master's, and doctoral degrees at Harvard, studying under Diana L. Eck and Kausalya Hart. She taught at the University of Virginia (1997–2002) and Harvard (2002–2019).

Anne Feldhaus is an indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Manhattanville College (circa 1967–1971) and earned her doctorate from the University of Pennsylvania (circa 1971–1976). In 1981, she joined Arizona State University, where she became Distinguished Foundation Professor and Emeritus Professor.

Anne Hardgrove specializes in history, archaeology, and indology. She studied at Carleton College and the University of Michigan (until 1999) and served as Redaktionsråd at the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000.

Anne M. Blackburn is a scholar of Buddhist studies, indology, and religious studies who completed graduate studies at the University of Chicago (1991). She held posts at Harvard University (circa 1999–2000), Cornell University (circa 2000), and the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).

Anne MacDonald is an indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida, Ashok Narhar Aklujkar, Geshe Tashi Namgyal, Lambert Schmithausen, and Karin Preisendanz. She has held posts at the University of Vienna and Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Anne Nishimura Morse is a scholar of Japanology, history, and archaeology who studied under John M. Rosenfield, Taka Yanagisawa, and Yutaka Hirata. She held posts at Smith College (1988–1989), Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (1988), Nara National Museum (1996), and Kyoto National Museum (1998).

Anne Ruth Hansen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and religious studies who studied under Charles Hallisey. She held an affiliation at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (attested 2007) and has served as professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison (attested 2012–2026).
Anne-Marie Blondeau is a tibetologist who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. She held an academic post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Annegret Bollée was a linguist who studied at the University of Hamburg (circa 1957–1961), Aix-Marseille University (circa 1961–1963), and the University of Bonn (1969).

Annemarie Schimmel was an indologist and religious studies scholar who earned doctorates at Humboldt University and the University of Marburg under Friedrich Heiler, Hans Ellenberg, and Hans Heinrich Schaeder. She held professorships at Marburg, Ankara University (1954–1967), and Harvard University (1967–1992).

Annemarie von Gabain was a scholar of Central Asian studies, linguistics, and archaeology who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1920–1925). She held posts at Humboldt University (circa 1935–1945) and as professor at the University of Hamburg (circa 1950–1966).

Annette Baier was a philosopher who studied at the University of Otago (circa 1946–1952) and Somerville College (PhD 1952). She taught at Carnegie Mellon University (circa 1968–1973) and the University of Pittsburgh's philosophy department (circa 1973–1995).

Annette L. Heitmann is a scholar in tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1987–1989) and completed her doctoral degree at the University of Vienna in 2002, studying under Christian Lindtner and David Seyfort Ruegg.

Annette Schmiedchen is an indologist and historian who earned her PhD at Humboldt University and completed her Habilitation at MLU Halle-Wittenberg, where she was a faculty member (circa 1996–2009). She has held appointments at Humboldt University, JNU, and the IASS.

Annie Besant was an indology and religious studies figure who studied at Birkbeck, University of London (circa 1879–1883). She founded Banaras Hindu University in 1898, serving as its president, and was president of the Theosophical Society (circa 1907–1933).

Anthony C. Yu was a sinologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (PhD 1969). He spent his career at the University of Chicago (circa 1968–2005) as a distinguished service professor.

Anthony Cerulli is a scholar of indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Chicago from 2001 to 2007. Around 2014, he served as Professor of South Asian Studies and Director of Graduate Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Leiden University in 1928 under J. J. L. Duyvendak, whom he later succeeded, serving as a lecturer in Chinese from 1946 and as professor from 1956 to 1975.

Anthony Tribe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and indology who studied at the University of Bristol and earned a DPhil at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, Steven Collins, and Paul Williams. He held posts at the University of Montana and University of Arizona.
